Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: MedScope POC — initial availability and network notes

Thanks for the call earlier. Samantha and I regrouped and want to get the hands-on sprint scheduled next week. A few quick constraints from our side:

- We have a maintenance window on 2027-04-19 between 02:00–06:00 PDT (can't do demos in that window).
- Our security team will need the VPC allowlist and IP ranges at least 48 hours before the session.
- We can provide two sandbox service accounts (non-prod) and a staging endpoint for testing.

Proposed slots (PDT):
- Tue 2027-04-20: 09:00–11:30
- Tue 2027-04-20: 14:00–16:00
- Wed 2027-04-21: 10:00–12:00

Can you confirm which slot works and whether you need additional artifacts (e.g., sample prompts, routing matrix, load test script)?

Thanks,
Tom

Lead DevOps Engineer | MedScope Health

Subject: Re: MedScope POC — initial availability and network notes

Thanks Tom — great summary. We can absolutely meet the 48-hour allowlist requirement. Quick asks from our side so the hands-on sprint is productive:

- Can you share the sandbox account IDs and confirm whether the staging endpoint requires mTLS or just IP allowlist?
- We'll do a focused prompt review before the session — can Samantha share 3 representative prompts and the success criteria?
- Ben and I recommend a single 2.5-hour working session rather than two shorter slots to preserve context. If you prefer morning, Tue 09:00–11:30 PDT works for us.

Deliverables we'll send before the session:
- Redwood POC checklist (high level runbook) [Attachment: POC-Checklist.pdf]
- Network allowlist template [Attachment: network-allowlist-template.csv]
- A short load test plan (token-level simulated traffic)

I'll tentatively book Tue 2027-04-20 09:00–11:30 PDT and send a calendar invite; please confirm and provide the sandbox details.

—Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Morning Stephanie — Tue 09:00–11:30 PDT is good for us. Quick notes on prompts:

- Prompt A: clinical triage summary extraction (short examples attached)
- Prompt B: policy-compliant patient data redaction
- Prompt C: specialty routing classifier (cardiology vs. orthopedics)

Success criteria:
- Extraction F1 > 0.85 on the sample set
- Redaction should remove PHI tokens in >95% of cases
- Routing precision >90% for top-1 classification

I'll upload the representative prompt set and sample responses to the Drive link you shared. We'll also add sandbox account IDs there.

—Samantha

Product Manager | MedScope Health

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Cc: rachel_kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 07:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MedScope POC — initial availability and network notes

Heads up — I switched the workshop agenda to include a short 'routing & fallback' demo and a 20-minute load test at the end. Things we'll need from MedScope before the session:

- Staging endpoint URL(s) and whether they require basic auth/mTLS
- API key(s) for sandbox accounts (or scoped API tokens)
- Any rate-limiting proxy in front of the staging endpoint (we need to know token/sec caps)

Agenda (2.5 hours):
1) 09:00–09:15 introductions & scope
2) 09:15–10:00 prompt review and prompt engineering notes
3) 10:00–10:30 routing, model variant selection, and fallback policies
4) 10:30–10:50 short integration tests (sanity checks)
5) 10:50–11:10 load test (steady-state ~50 r/s simulated)
6) 11:10–11:30 review results & next steps

We can adapt the load profile based on what the staging infrastructure can handle. If you can't share API keys over email, we can do a screen-share for a one-time token exchange at session start.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: sample-load-profile.json (JSON)]

From: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, rachel_kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@medscope.com>, Samantha Li <samantha.li@medscope.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MedScope POC — initial availability and network notes

Small update: I ran a quick baseline against a sandbox model we host and prepared a short token-cost estimate and quantization recommendation for the session. Notes below:

- If MedScope intends to exercise long-context prompts (>1k tokens), we'll show a 2x latency delta between the float32 path and the int8-quantized path — we should demonstrate both.
- For the load test, target 30–50 r/s with batching size 8 to simulate a realistic throughput profile; we'll throttle if the staging endpoint signals backpressure.
- I attached a short runbook excerpt with the commands we'll run during the load test.

I'll join the call from my lab environment; please confirm the staging URL and whether we should use the provided sandbox API keys or request ephemeral tokens at start.

—Priyom
Priyom Das
Applied ML Engineer | Redwood Inference
